cards.text: This one's a psalm of David, the servant of the LORD, written for the choirmaster. David says he's got an oracle in his heart about the transgression of the wicked man. And he opens with it: "There is no fear of God before his eyes."

cards.question: There's no fear of God before the wicked man's eyes. So why can't he spot his own sin?

answers.text: His eyes are too full of conceit
His friends cover it up for him

cards.text: He's too full of himself to see his sin, let alone hate it. That's a man admiring his reflection in the oven door while the batch right behind it BURNS.

cards.question: David says the wicked man's words are wicked and deceitful, but he's still wise and still does good.
David says the wicked man's scheming never clocks out. Where does he plot wickedness?

cards.text: On his BED? I lie down and the only thing I plot is how many times I'm hitting snooze, and this man's in there drawing up blueprints for trouble.

cards.question: David says the wicked man sets himself on a good path and only slips off it now and then.

cards.text: Then the psalm turns, HARD. David takes his eyes off the wicked man and starts talking straight to the LORD.

cards.question: David starts with the LORD's loving devotion. How far does he say it reaches?

answers.text: To the ends of the earth
To the far side of the sea

cards.text: And His faithfulness reaches to the clouds. David's grabbing the biggest things he can find to describe the LORD.

cards.question: David says God's righteousness is like the highest mountains, and His judgments are like the deepest ___.
David says the LORD preserves people but leaves the animals on their own.

cards.text: Heavens. Clouds. Mountains. The deepest sea. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer you couldn't fit a rolling pin in, and David needs the WHOLE SKY just to get started on the LORD.
David keeps going: God's loving devotion is precious. So precious that the children of men take refuge in Him.

cards.question: What picture does David use for the place where people take refuge in God?
David says the people who take refuge in God get only the leftovers from His house.

cards.text: They feast on the abundance of God's house, and He gives them drink from His river of delights. A RIVER of delights, and I still get emotional when the chocolate chips come in the big bag.

cards.question: David gives the reason for all this good: with God is the fountain of ___.

cards.text: And then: "in Your light we see light." After all that praise, David turns it into a prayer.

cards.question: David asks God to keep His loving devotion coming. Who does he ask God to extend it to?

cards.text: He asks for God's righteousness to reach the upright in heart too. Then David's mind goes back to the proud and the wicked.

cards.question: What does David ask God about the proud and the wicked?

answers.text: Don't let them drive me away

cards.question: David closes with a picture: the evildoers lie fallen, thrown down and unable to ___.

cards.text: The psalm opened with the wicked man lying on his bed, plotting. It closes with the evildoers lying fallen, and they can't get back up.

findings.problem: The question says David claims the wicked man's scheming "never clocks out." Psalm 36:4 only says "Even on his bed he plots wickedness." The card makes it sound like David says the plotting never stops, which goes beyond the text.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: "How far does he say it reaches?" asks the baker to supply the next words of Psalm 36:5 ("reaches to the heavens"). Nothing on card 8 points toward the heavens, so this is a wording guess and not a question about movement or meaning.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The blank in "His judgments are like the deepest ___" is the next word of the line in Psalm 36:6, and no story card sets it up. A baker reasoning from "highest mountains" could also argue for "valley" as the opposite of mountains, so the blank tests unseen wording, not meaning.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The card lists "Heavens. Clouds. Mountains. The deepest sea." which repeats what cards 9 to 12 already covered and adds no new part of Psalm 36:5-6. It is a recap with a joke attached. It doesn't move the passage forward.

The question asks about "the proud and the wicked," but the right answer "Don't let them drive me away" is true only of the wicked. Psalm 36:11 asks that the foot of the proud not come against him, and that the hand of the wicked not drive him away.

rule.text: A card about two groups needs an answer true for both. When a question covers more than one group, like the sea creatures and the birds, the right answer must be true for every group in it.

findings.problem: The card goes back to the wicked man on his bed from verse 4 and repeats card 10's answer ("they can't get back up"). It tells no new part of the passage. It is a recap card.
